newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE KEEP MONACO WAITING FOR TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE KEEP MONACO WAITING FOR TITLE.

text.p: Monaco will have to wait before celebrating their first title for a decade after the French league leaders drew at home with Marseille on Saturday.
A header from Sylvain Legwinski after 62 minutes allowed Monaco to share the points and take a 12-point lead over second-placed Paris St Germain.
But it will not be enough for Monaco to be mathematically certain of collecting their first crown since 1988 if the Parisians beat bottom-of-the-table Nice on Sunday.

A win would almost have done the job. But Monaco had to fight back from one goal down after Xavier Gravelaine opened the scoring in the 35th minute and the league leaders missed too many easy chances in the second half.
Midfielder Ali Benarbia, for one, found himself on his own in front of an empty goal with three minutes left but shot wide.
"Now we must win in Strasbourg or against Caen but the most important thing today was not to lose after a very hard match a couple of days ago," said coach Jean Tigana.
In the first half, Monaco -- looking a little weary after their 10th UEFA Cup match, a second leg semifinal against Internazionale on Tuesday -- did not look like a team in sight of a title.
They dominated for half an hour but to little effect and a fine shot from Brazilian Sonny Anderson in the 21st minute was Monaco's only real chance.
Goalkeeper Jerome Alonzo, standing in for Marseille's injured German international Andreas Koepke who was watching the match from the stands, made a fine save.
Marseille then decided to take the game to Monaco and Bulgaria's Yordan Lechkov was ideally placed on the right side of the box in the 31st minute but he crossed to Marc Libbra instead of shooting..
Four minutes later veteran Bernard Ferrer broke through Monaco's defence and launched Gravelaine behind the backs.
The striker had only to dribble past goalkeeper Fabien Barthez to score from the left.
Things improved radically for Monaco in the second half and after 17 minutes of constant pressure Legwinski nodded home from a corner taken by Benarbia.
The goal gave Monaco a lift and they kept up the pressure on Marseille until the final whistle. But Alonzo, arguably the best player on the pitch, kept them at bay.
Marseille coach Gerard Gili said: "We took four out of six points against Monaco. It sums up our season. We had our best results against the best teams."
Monaco lost 3-1 away to Marseille in November. On Saturday they maintined their unbeaten home record in the league, while Marseille are still looking for their first win away.

Monaco - 1-Fabien Barthez; 2-Patrick Blondeau, 18-Gilles Grimandi, 5-Franck Dumas (captain), 19-Lilian Martin (17-Philippe Leonard 60); 15-Sylvain Legwinski, 4-Martin Djetou (14-Laurent Viaud 63), 8-Ali Benarbia, 6-Emmanuel Petit; 9-Sonny Anderson, 12-Thierry Henry.

Marseille - 16-Jerome Alonzo; 25-Hamada Jambay, 19-Christophe Galtier (captain), 4-Alberto Malusci, 2-Chris Makin; 18-Olivier Echouafni, 6-Eric Roy, 10-Yordan Lechkov (23-Marcial Robin 71), 13-Bernard Ferrer; 24-Marc Libbra, 11-Xavier Gravelaine.
